record.title: KAPPO derives adaptive policy pressure for pass@k and max@k post-training
record.summary: The authors derive closed-form optimal policies for KL-regularized pass@k and max@k objectives and identify prompt-adaptive pressure that can be implemented by modifying standard @1 optimization. They report experiments on mathematical reasoning and code generation using OLMo-3-7B-Instruct-SFT and Qwen3-4B-Base: KAPPO variants reduce the paper's measured sharpening pattern, and @k-A*PO using one new completion per prompt is reported comparable to PKPO, which requires at least k on-policy completions. These are paper-reported results, not independent reproductions.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper derives closed-form optimal policies for KL-regularized pass@k and max@k objectives and expresses their optimization pressure through prompt-adaptive regularization or reward transformations.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that KAPPO adaptations reduce sharpening in experiments on mathematical reasoning and code generation with OLMo-3-7B-Instruct-SFT and Qwen3-4B-Base.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that @k-A*PO using one new completion per prompt reaches validation performance comparable to PKPO, which uses at least k new on-policy completions per prompt.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish that KAPPO improves production training cost or transfers to other model families, tasks, or reward regimes.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors state that Qwen's pretraining cutoff is undocumented and contamination of the LiveCodeBench evaluation cannot be ruled out completely.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of KAPPO's reported sharpening and rollout-cost results was located or performed; the supplementary code and checkpoints were not inspected.
Generalization beyond the two model families and selected mathematics/code tasks remains untested in the inspected paper.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported effect generalizes, adapting common single-completion policy optimizers to pass@k/max@k objectives could reduce rollout requirements while retaining broader solution coverage on difficult tasks. That could change practical post-training choices, but the scale is bounded: evidence is author-reported on two model families and selected math/code settings, with calibration and reward-surrogate limitations.
limitations: All experimental results are reported by the paper authors and have not been independently reproduced in this activation.
The mathematics experiments use two model families and AIME 2026; the code experiments use Qwen3-4B-Base and the hard subset of LiveCodeBench v6.
The reference calibration uses a static bank of M completions per prompt; the paper says this can make estimates noisier.
For continuous rewards, experiments optimize a win-rate surrogate rather than directly evaluating raw-reward max@k optimization.
The authors state that applying the win-rate solution to discrete rewards with ties is an approximation.
The paper states that Qwen's pretraining cutoff is undocumented, so LiveCodeBench contamination cannot be ruled out completely.
brief.summary: The authors derive closed-form optimal policies for KL-regularized pass@k and max@k objectives and identify prompt-adaptive pressure that can be implemented by modifying standard @1 optimization. They report experiments on mathematical reasoning and code generation using OLMo-3-7B-Instruct-SFT and Qwen3-4B-Base: KAPPO variants reduce the paper's measured sharpening pattern, and @k-A*PO using one new completion per prompt is reported comparable to PKPO, which requires at least k on-policy completions. These are paper-reported results, not independent reproductions.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report reduced sharpening for @k-A*PO, @k-DPO and @k-GRPO on mathematical reasoning and code generation. In reported comparisons, one-new-completion @k-A*PO is comparable to PKPO, a dedicated pass@k optimizer requiring at least k new on-policy completions per prompt.
technical.compute_or_cost: The rollout-cost comparison is based on one new completion per prompt for the reported @k-A*PO setup versus at least k for PKPO. End-to-end compute, calibration-bank cost and production serving economics were not independently measured here.
technical.demonstrated_result: The publication event and the contents of the paper are directly inspectable. Experimental outcomes remain author-reported claims and are not independently demonstrated here.
technical.implementation_status: Paper includes pseudocode and says the code base is in supplementary materials; this activation did not inspect or run the supplement.
technical.mechanism: For KL-regularized pass@k and max@k objectives, the paper derives closed-form optimal policies and shows that their pressure can be represented through prompt-adaptive regularization or reward transformations. KAPPO uses a one-time reference calibration and adjusts existing @1 optimizers.
technical.novelty: A closed-form connection between KL-regularized @k objectives and prompt-adaptive pressure provides a route to adapt existing @1 optimizers without online multi-completion learning signals.
technical.regime: Mathematics: RL on MATH training data, validation on the MATH test split, final evaluation on AIME 2026 with OLMo-3-7B-Instruct-SFT and Qwen3-4B-Base. Code: Qwen3-4B-Base trained on the LeetCodeDataset training split, validation on its test split, and final evaluation on the hard subset of LiveCodeBench v6.
technical.reproducibility: Full arXiv v1 PDF inspected. No independent reproduction was found or attempted; supplementary code/checkpoints were not inspected. Qwen's pretraining cutoff is undocumented, so the authors state LiveCodeBench contamination cannot be ruled out completely.
technical.strongest_baseline: For binary-reward mathematics, the paper compares k-adjusted A*PO with k=1 A*PO/GRPO and PKPO on OLMo-3-7B-Instruct-SFT and Qwen3-4B-Base. For continuous-reward code generation, it compares k=1,2,4 variants on Qwen3-4B-Base.

brief.title: KAPPO derives adaptive policy pressure for pass@k and max@k post-training
brief.why_it_matters: If reproduced, adaptive pressure could let existing single-completion policy optimizers target pass@k/max@k behavior with fewer new rollouts than methods that collect k completions per prompt. The paper also gives an optimizer-independent derivation connecting @k objectives to prompt-adaptive regularization or reward transformation. The evidence is limited to two model families and the reported task setups; it does not establish production cost savings or transfer to arbitrary models and tasks.
